summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled with prior DKA admissions, alcohol use disorder, depression, and hypertension presented with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. She was found to be in diabetic ketoacidosis with a blood glucose of 706 and a pH of 6.9, likely due to not taking her sliding scale insulin after losing access to her glucometer, compounded by recent heavy alcohol use. She was treated with IV fluids, an insulin drip, and electrolyte repletion in the ICU. Her condition improved rapidly, with resolution of DKA, normalization of kidney function, and stabilization of vital signs. T-wave inversions on EKG were noted but attributed to demand ischemia from metabolic stress rather than acute coronary syndrome. She was transitioned back to her home insulin regimen, provided with a new glucometer, and discharged home with follow-up instructions. Social work was involved to support ongoing alcohol use counseling.
